title: Kirk 2012

pages.message: Hurricanes tend to form over the warm tropical oceans where the SST is warmer than ~26.5 C (~80 F)

These simple visualizations are plots of time vs. wind speed for each tropical storm/hurricane of Atlantic Hurricane seasons from 1950 to the present. Horizontal lines indicate wind speed category thresholds.

note: Ours: Grows over warm water and weakens as it moves north into cold water: the SST under it falls 7.7 °C in a day. No landfall. The whole life of the storm (section 12); SST is the monthly mean under its centre, empty over land. The Atlantic's neutral SST, where storms neither strengthen nor weaken on average over the next 24 hours, is 26.9 °C (section 5.1).

sources.source: HURDAT2 Atlantic best track (NOAA National Hurricane Center)
sources.credit: Landsea, C. W. and J. L. Franklin, 2013: Atlantic Hurricane Database Uncertainty and Presentation of a New Database Format. Mon. Wea. Rev., 141, 3576-3592.

title: Lee 2017

pages.message: Hurricanes tend to form over the warm tropical oceans where the SST is warmer than ~26.5 C (~80 F)

These simple visualizations are plots of time vs. wind speed for each tropical storm/hurricane of Atlantic Hurricane seasons from 1950 to the present. Horizontal lines indicate wind speed category thresholds.

note: Ours: Drifts weak for nine days, falls apart and comes back, grows over warm water east of Bermuda and weakens as it races north-east into cold water: the SST under it falls 7.9 °C in a day. No landfall. The whole life of the storm (section 12); SST is the monthly mean under its centre, empty over land. The Atlantic's neutral SST, where storms neither strengthen nor weaken on average over the next 24 hours, is 26.9 °C (section 5.1).
